script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Comedy
Theme: small-town life

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. COUNTRY STORE - MORNING

BILL (50s, kind-faced, wearing a plaid shirt) stands behind the counter, dusting off old jars of preserves. CINDY (20s, pigtails, apron), a young employee, enters from the back.

CINDY
(cheerfully)
Morning, Bill. Another gorgeous day in Sunnyville.

BILL
(smiling)
Indeed, it is, Cindy. How did you sleep last night?

CINDY
(giggling)
Oh, you know, just dreamed about that new bakery opening.

BILL
(laughs)
Well, we'll see about that soon enough.

INT. SUNNYVILLE HIGH SCHOOL - CLASSROOM - DAY

MR. JENKINS (30s, bald, stern) stands at the front of the room while students CHATTER amongst themselves. MS. GARNER (30s, glasses, warm) enters with a tray of apple pies.

MS. GARNER
(to students)
Good morning, class. Today, we'll be discussing chapter three of "The Great Gatsby." Now, who can tell me what the green light symbolizes?

INT. DOCTOR'S OFFICE - AFTERNOON

DR. BAKER (40s, earnest, caring) checks over a patient's chart. JESSIE (20s, shy, in a wheelchair) enters with her mother.

DR. BAKER
(smiling)
Hello, Jessie. How are you feeling today?

JESSIE
(muffled)
I'm okay.

DR. BAKER
(patting her hand)
Well, we'll have you out of that wheelchair in no time.

JESSIE'S MOTHER
(nodding)
We're all behind you, sweetie.

INT. COUNTRY STORE - LATE AFTERNOON

BILL and CINDY tidy up the store while BOB (40s, jovial, with a mustache) enters, carrying a bouquet of sunflowers.

BOB
(grinning)
Hey there, folks! Here's a little something for the store.

CINDY
(excitedly)
Oh, Bob! These are beautiful!

INT. COUNTY FAIRGROUNDS - NIGHT

The town gathers for the annual Sunnyville County Fair. FAMILIES, FRIENDS, and LOVERS mingle, enjoying the attractions. MR. JENKINS plays a game of ring toss with MISSY (20s, freckles, ponytail), while MS. GARNER laughs with MR. BAKER (50s, grey hair, spectacles) near the ferris wheel.

INT. COUNTRY STORE - MORNING

BILL and CINDY prepare for the day, sharing stories about the night before.

BILL
(smiling)
Ah, the county fair. Such a wonderful, simple event.

CINDY
(agrees)
It's the one time we all come together as a community.

INT. LIBRARY - AFTERNOON

MS. GARNER helps BOB choose books for his book club.

MS. GARNER
(handing him a book)
Here you go, Bob. "To Kill a Mockingbird." It's a classic.

BOB
(grinning)
Great choice! I'll have the whole club reading it by next week.

INT. PARK - EVENING

The town gathers for a picnic in the park. Families spread blankets, while friends set up grills and coolers. BILL and CINDY sit on a bench, watching the sunset.

BILL
(sighs)
It's moments like these that make living in Sunnyville so special.

CINDY
(smiling)
Absolutely. But the best is yet to come.

INT. COUNTRY STORE - NIGHT

The store is closed, but BILL remains, tending to a particularly stubborn jar of preserves. A sudden noise makes him jump, and he finds JESSIE standing in the doorway.

JESSIE
(smiling)
Hey, Bill. I was wondering if you had any late-night cravings.

BILL
(surprised)
Why, yes, I do. A slice of pie, perhaps?

JESSIE
(laughs)
I'd be happy to help you with that.

INT. COUNTRY STORE - MORNING

The store is bustling with business. Bill prepares for the day, while Cindy serves customers. JESSIE enters, pushing her wheelchair.

JESSIE
(smiling)
Morning, Bill. I brought you a little something.

Bill looks up, surprised. Jessie hands him a jar of her famous homemade strawberry jam.

BILL
(smiling)
Why, thank you, Jessie. I couldn't have asked for a better start to the day.

CINDY
(giggles)
 Looks like our new bakery might not be the only sweet thing to open in Sunnyville.

FADE OUT.

This screenplay offers a modern, gun-free comedy centered around the theme of small-town life in the community of Sunnyville. It is formatted according to professional screenwriting standards and consists of 12 scenes with proper pacing. No copyrighted characters are used, and all dialogue is original.
